findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIRD REPEAT- There was a pan of raw beef above a container of carrots in the bottom of the preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The beef was moved to the bottom and the carrots were moved above the raw beef. Due to this being a third repeat violation, the inspector will bring the health educator to the facility for education on storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT- There was observed to be raw pork belly on a package of imitation crab meat. CORRECTED- The raw pork belly was moved to be on another shelf and the PIC was educated on proper storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Proper storage order should be as follows: 
1. Ready-to-Eat Foods. 
2. Unwashed fruits and vegetables. 
3. Partially cooked foods (ex: par-cooked chicken). 
4. Seafood and shell eggs. 
5. Beef and Pork. 
6. Chicken.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was a dented can of oyster sauce that was observed to be in the bottom of the preparation cooler. The can was dented along the bottom seam and oyster sauce was being stored in it to be used. CORRECTED- The can and oyster sauce in it were both voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Education was conducted regarding dented cans. Dented cans should never be used and should be set apart from all other food. These dented cans can be returned to the distributor. Dents in cans means that the integrity of the can has been compromised and the food is exposed to contamination.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of cooked meat observed to not have a date on it in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Date-marking was discussed with the PIC. The PIC stated that the meat was cooked yesterday and a date was placed on it by the PIC. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are date-marked with day one being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the seventh day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: The bleach that is being used to make sanitizer in the facility is observed to not have an EPA Registration Number. This was discussed with the PIC and education was conducted on the correct type to get. It is important that the bleach has the EPA Registration Number on it to ensure that it is safe to be used on food contact surfaces and is properly sanitizing food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- The PIC obtained bleach with an EPA Registration Number during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

6-403.11: In the walk-in cooler, there is personal storage above food that is intended to serve for consumers. Personal storage should be on the bottom shelf or away from food intended for the restaurant. Cease use of this space for personal storage and move these items. 

 (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Employees were observed switching tasks without washing their hands before engaging in food preparation activities again. This behavior was brought to the attention of the PIC and was corrected via verbal education. Ensure hands are washed properly when switching tasks and engaging in food handling practices. This is a repeat violation from the 9/26/2024 inspection and the facility will be receiving a repeat letter documenting the violation. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: The wiping cloth was observed stored on the prep table between uses. This was brought to the PIC’s attention and education was given to the other employee to keep the rag in the santiizer bucket between uses. 
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The external portion of the door including the handles of the prep cooler were observed to have an accumulation of food soil/debris. PIC was made aware and will be cleaning and sanitizing this surface. Ensure this surface is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The main kitchen chest freezer is observed that the gasket of the unit is coming apart. PIC was made aware and will be performing repairs to these units or will replace the seals. This is a repeated violation from the 9/26/2023 inspection and the facility will be receiving a letter documenting the violation.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: At the start of the inspection, a sanitizer rag was observed stored in the basin of the hand sink. This rag was removed at the start of the inspection and placed back into the freshly made sanitizer bucket. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The hood system is observed to have an accumulation of grease/debris that has formed droplets and is observed to be dripping. PIC was made aware of this and is in the process of cleaning these surfaces during the inspection. Although PIC removes and cleans the baffles regularly, ensure that the drip catch tray is cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the system from dripping onto the cook surfaces below.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: The prep cooler was observed at the start of the inspection to not have a hanging thermometer present in the cooler. An extra thermometer was available in the facility and placed into this cooler. Ensure all coolers in the facility have an internal thermometer separate form the display thermometer that comes with the equipment.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The ice dispenser for the soda machine was soiled with mildew and other debris. Ensure the ice machine dispenser is cleaned frequently so it is maintained clean to sight and touch. The dispenser was cleaned immediately during the inspection. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The prep cooler was cold holding foods at approximately 48F. The manager stated the cooler was stocked recently and was open a lot over lunch. The cooler was dropping in temperature by the end of the inspection. The TCS foods (eggs, chicken, beef) are usually used within 2-3 hours. Ensure the prep cooler temperature is maintained at 41F or below.  EG will check the prep cooler in a day or two to ensure the prep cooler is functioning properly. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Meats were observed thawing improperly. The chicken was submerged in a container full of water with no running water into the container. Food must be thawed under cold, running water if submerged in water. The faucet was turned on to allow cold, running water to pour into the container during the thawing process. Thawing methods were discussed with employees. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
A fly strip with flies on it was observed hanging from the ceiling over the prep table. Ensure fly strips are not hung over food or food equipment to protect food and food-contact surfaces from contamination. 

6-202.13: (B) Devices shall be installed where it is not located over FOOD preparation area and dead insects and fragments cannot impel or fall into exposed FOOD or FOOD-EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The burner next to the fryer and the side of the fryer was soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent the accumulations of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The manager’s CFPM certificate was expired. Ensure the license is renewed. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizer bucket to test at 0 ppm for chlorine. Chlorine concentrations in sanitizer solutions must be maintained between 50ppm and 200ppm. The bucket was remade during inspection to correct the violation and had a concentration of 100ppm of chlorine. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11: Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with black debris. Baffle of ice machine was cleaned and sanitized. (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: 3-501.19: Observed that no use by time was indicated for par-cooked chicken and egg rolls. Proper use by time was recorded by PIC. (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.
